brief: UBS flags choppy US rates and equities as mixed AI signals combine with persistent inflation: September PPI rose 1.3% month on month, the sharpest gain in four and a half years and well above a 0.5% consensus, with gains broadening beyond energy, following a higher-than-expected CPI print earlier in the week. Even so, the 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 5.09%, near a three-week low, as equity volatility lifted demand for high-quality bonds. UBS argues the market's pricing of Fed tightening (nearly 90bp over 12 months) is too hawkish; it forecasts only 50bp more, in December and March, then a hold through late 2027, pointing to dovish comments from Fed officials Jefferson, Williams and Daly, and expects yields to decline as pricing adjusts. Fed Chair Warsh's remarks cut implied odds of an October hike to under 15% from 27%, lifting S&P futures and weakening the dollar. UBS rates fixed income Attractive for its income cushion and diversification versus equities, but stays cautious on the longest maturities on fiscal concerns and AI-driven issuance. It also raises its Brent forecast to $100 on Ukraine's refinery strike, continuing Iran-linked Gulf attacks, and a larger-than-expected US crude draw tied to hurricane-disrupted Gulf output.
